blocks.text: BRISBANE — Bedridden by her late 20s and “laughed out of doctors’ offices,” Jessica Birch waited years to receive a life-changing diagnosis. Now she is sharing her story to help the more than one million Australians estimated to be affected by her lifelong condition. Ms Birch is speaking out as part of national efforts to destigmatize Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder, or FASD, and raise awareness of available support. She hopes her lived experience and advocacy will save others years of being “horrendously gaslit.” FASD is a physical and neurodevelopmental condition caused by prenatal alcohol exposure.
